chose: One voice policy for every essay kind (voices.ts), a union of two cases. `fixed` is one voice per speaker for the whole video: what every version before it says, byte for byte, and the weekly call's, whose sections each have their own voice already. `lanes` gives each role (host, narrator, tutor, asker, answerer) its own lane of three Kokoro voices, disjoint from the other lanes. A role's voice in chapter c is its lane's c-th, round robin, so it holds for a chapter and changes at each boundary, two roles never share a voice, and the same essay always gets the same voices. A chapter is what the video marks: a chapter slide in an essay, a chapter mark in a cards essay, a spoken card included. So an exchange sits within one chapter, and its asker and answerer keep their voices through it. The lanes are turned on by a `voices: "lanes-v1"` field in a template's shape and a series, as C822 turned on the cast, so a pinned version never changes voice. The Rust essay's version 7, the interview essay's version 4 and cheat-sheet's version 4 name the lanes, and the routine pins cheat-sheet 4. The call stays `fixed`: the lanes would rotate its host, so they don't subsume its per-section voices, and its output is unchanged. The pool is the English voices home's speaker loads (Kokoro-FastAPI v0.9.2, voices/v1_0). Each lane holds the better-sounding ones. The host's opens on the call's host, so the intro sounds as it did, and the narrator's is ordered so a cards essay's first card (its chapter 1) is still narrated in af_heart; the tutor's, asker's and answerer's old voices are taken by those two, so their lanes are new voices.
options: a lane per role, disjoint, round robin by chapter (chosen)
one shared pool, each role offset by its place: a voice can pass from one role to the next across a boundary, so a listener hears the narrator become the host
random per chapter, seeded by the essay: deterministic too, but two chapters in a row can land on the same voice
rotate the call's sections too: changes a weekly call's voices that the owner already enjoys
gray: Which voices the owner hears, and where they change, is on the screen; no check settled the lanes' members or what counts as a chapter.
undo: Drop `voices` from the shapes, the series schema and cheat-sheet v4, delete rust-essay/v7.json and cheat-sheet/v4.json, set ESSAY_VERSION back to 6 and INTERVIEW_ESSAY_VERSION to 3, and the policy's `fixed` case says what every essay said before. Essays written at the newer versions are then refused (VS1).
